claim: dbd-Gal4 first expresses in dbd neurons at embryonic stage 14.
source: We observed the first expression of dbd-Gal4 in dbd neurons at embryonic stage 14.
evidence: Direct observation from immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 1A

claim: At embryonic stage 14, dbd axons have just entered the dorsal central nervous system (CNS) as immature growth cones.
source: At this time, the axons have just entered the dorsal central nervous system (CNS) as immature growth cones (Figure 1A)
evidence: Observation from stage 14 embryo imaging shown in Figure 1A

claim: At embryonic stage 14, dbd axons would not yet have contacted the more ventral neuropil domain occupied by the A08a dendrites.
source: At this time, the axons have just entered the dorsal central nervous system (CNS) as immature growth cones (Figure 1A), and would not yet have contacted the more ventral neuropil domain occupied by the A08a dendrites.
evidence: Inference based on the dorsal position of dbd axons at stage 14 and the known ventral location of A08a dendrites

claim: By embryonic stage 15, dbd neurons formed anterior/posterior bilateral branches adjacent to the midline of the neuropil.
source: By stage 15, the dbd neurons formed anterior/posterior bilateral branches adjacent to the midline of the neuropil (Figure 1B)
evidence: Direct observation from stage 15 embryo imaging shown in Figure 1B

claim: By embryonic stage 17, dbd axon terminals further elaborated to link adjacent segments.
source: By stage 15, the dbd neurons formed anterior/posterior bilateral branches adjacent to the midline of the neuropil (Figure 1B), followed by further elaboration to link adjacent segments in stage 17 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Direct observation from stage 17 embryo imaging shown in Figure 1C

claim: By embryonic stage 17, dbd axon terminals occupy a more ventral region of the neuropil where A08a medial dendrites are formed.
source: By this time, dbd axon terminals occupy a more ventral region of the neuropil where A08a medial dendrites are formed (Schrader and Merritt, 2000; Zlatic et al., 2003).
evidence: Observation from stage 17 embryos combined with citations to previous literature on A08a dendrite location

claim: A08a-LexA first labels A08a in the early hours of the first larval instar.
source: This line first labels A08a in the early hours of the first larval instar (Figure 1D and F).
evidence: Direct observation from larval imaging at 2±2 hr after larval hatching shown in Figure 1D

claim: By the time A08a-LexA first labels A08a, A08a has contacted dbd and has developed its characteristic lateral and medial dendritic arbors.
source: By this time, A08a has contacted dbd and has developed its characteristic lateral and medial dendritic arbors.
evidence: Observation from early larval imaging at 2±2 hr after larval hatching

claim: dbd-Gal4 labels the dbd sensory neuron prior to its growth into the A08a neuropil domain.
source: However, we conclude that dbd-Gal4 labels the dbd sensory neuron prior to its growth into the A08a neuropil domain, and thus it is an appropriate tool for manipulating dbd prior to the establishment of dbd-A08a synaptic connectivity.
evidence: Inference based on the timing of dbd-Gal4 expression at stage 14 when axons are immature growth cones in the dorsal CNS

claim: When dbd was targeted to intermediate or lateral neuropil domains, A08a produced an ectopic dendritic arbor to match the presynaptic contact.
source: Surprisingly, when dbd was targeted to lateral or intermediate neuropil domains, A08a produced an ectopic dendritic arbor to match the presynaptic contact (Valdes-Aleman et al., 2021).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Valdes-Aleman et al., 2021

claim: The cumulative distribution of A08a dendrite volume corresponds to the location of dbd input.
source: Here, we extended and confirmed these findings by showing that the cumulative distribution of A08a dendrite volume corresponds to the location of dbd input (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite volume distribution shown in Figure 2A-D

claim: When dbd was targeted to intermediate or lateral neuropil regions, the volume of the medial dendrite was decreased.
source: Interestingly, when dbd was targeted to intermediate or lateral neuropil regions, the volume of the medial dendrite was decreased (Figure 2D).
evidence: Quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: The increase in dendrite arbor volume was most striking in the intermediate zone of the A08a dendritic domain where there are few arbors present in wild type.
source: The increase in dendrite arbor volume was most striking in the intermediate zone of the A08a dendritic domain where there are few arbors present in wild type (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: Comparison of dendrite volume distributions between wild type and robo-2 conditions shown in Figure 2A-B

claim: When dbd is targeted to the intermediate zone, there is an increase in the frequency of dendritic branches off the primary A08a neurite in the intermediate zone.
source: We found that when dbd is targeted to the intermediate zone, there was an increase in the frequency of dendritic branches off the primary A08a neurite in the intermediate zone, supporting the idea that the observed increase in dendrite volume in the intermediate zone is due to novel dbd-promoted dendrite outgrowth (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of branch point distribution shown in Figure 2E-F

claim: Presynaptic contact can locally promote postsynaptic dendrite outgrowth.
source: We conclude that presynaptic contact can locally promote postsynaptic dendrite outgrowth, ultimately ensuring robust partner matching.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments showing ectopic dendrite formation when dbd is mistargeted

claim: Hid expression led to a loss of dbd neurons, as detected through the absence of both 22C10+ and HA+ cell bodies from the body wall.
source: Hid expression indeed led to a loss of dbd neurons, as detected through the absence of both 22C10+ and HA+ cell bodies from the body wall (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and D).
evidence: Validation experiments showing absence of dbd cell body markers in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and D

claim: Complete dbd ablation led to A08a lateral dendrites that were longer and more branched.
source: Quantification confirmed that complete dbd ablation led to A08a lateral dendrites that were longer and more branched (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite length and branching shown in Figure 3E-F

claim: There was no significant change in medial dendrite length or branching when dbd was ablated.
source: In contrast, there was no significant change in medial dendrite length or branching when dbd was ablated (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: Statistical analysis of medial dendrite measurements shown in Figure 3E-F

claim: When 1–2 of the 4 dbd neurons are ablated, A08a dendrite length is not significantly different than in controls.
source: We found that when 1–2 of the 4 dbd neurons are ablated, A08a dendrite length is not significantly different than in controls.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite length as a function of dbd neuron number shown in Figure 3G

claim: When 3–4 of the 4 dbd neurons are ablated, A08a lateral dendrite length is significantly increased.
source: However, when 3–4 of the 4 dbd neurons are ablated, A08a lateral dendrite length is significantly increased (Figure 3G).
evidence: Quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3G

claim: A threshold level rather than a linear summation of dbd input stabilizes A08a dendrite outgrowth.
source: This finding suggests that a threshold level rather than a linear summation of dbd input stabilizes A08a dendrite outgrowth.
evidence: Inference from the observation that dendrite length only changes when 3-4 of 4 dbd neurons are ablated

claim: dbd does not contact the lateral dendrite in wild-type animals.
source: The expansion of lateral A08a dendrite length was surprising, as dbd does not contact the lateral dendrite in wild-type animals (Sales et al., 2019; Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016).
evidence: Previously published findings from Sales et al., 2019 and Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016

claim: The growth in lateral dendrites following dbd ablation revealed that dbd provides negative regulation of A08a dendrite outgrowth.
source: The growth in lateral dendrites following dbd ablation revealed that dbd provides negative regulation of A08a dendrite outgrowth, in addition to the positive mechanism revealed by the dbd lateralization experiments.
evidence: Inference from the observation that lateral dendrites expand when dbd is ablated despite no direct contact

claim: The negative mechanism of dendrite regulation acts throughout the neuron, rather than locally as does the positive mechanism.
source: Moreover, the negative mechanism acts throughout the neuron, rather than locally as does the positive mechanism.
evidence: Inference from the observation that lateral dendrites are affected by dbd ablation despite no direct contact

claim: Based on the L1 larval TEM connectome, dbd and A08a neurons are among each other's strongest synaptic partners.
source: Based on the L1 larval TEM connectome, dbd and A08a neurons are among each other's strongest synaptic partners.
evidence: Analysis of published TEM connectome data

claim: For dbd, A08a ranks #6 among the top 10 synaptically connected 'downstream' neurons.
source: For dbd, the top 10 synaptically connected 'downstream' neurons are shown in Table 1, with A08a ranking #6
evidence: Analysis of TEM connectome data presented in Table 1

claim: For A08a, dbd is the #1 input neuron among the top 10 input neurons.
source: conversely, for A08a, the top 10 input neurons are shown in Table 2, with dbd being the #1 input to A08a (Tables 1 and 2; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Analysis of TEM connectome data presented in Table 2

claim: Based on synapse number and neurotransmitter identity, dbd is the major source of A08a excitation.
source: Based on synapse number and neurotransmitter identity, dbd is the major source of A08a excitation.
evidence: Inference from TEM connectome data showing dbd as top input and known cholinergic identity

claim: TNT cleaves the synaptic vesicle protein synaptobrevin, inhibiting evoked synaptic vesicle release.
source: TNT cleaves the synaptic vesicle protein synaptobrevin, inhibiting evoked synaptic vesicle release (Sweeney et al., 1995).
evidence: Established mechanism of TNT action cited from Sweeney et al., 1995

claim: dbd silencing led to slowed and uncoordinated larval locomotion.
source: A previous study showed that dbd silencing led to slowed and uncoordinated larval locomotion (Hughes and Thomas, 2007).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Hughes and Thomas, 2007

claim: Dbd-silenced animals had fewer waves of crawling activity.
source: Dbd-silenced animals had fewer waves of crawling activity, consistent with the previous results (Figure 4A–B and E).
evidence: Behavioral analysis shown in Figure 4A-B and E

claim: Constitutive dbd silencing using TNT resulted in longer, more branched lateral and medial A08a dendrites at 26±2 hr alh.
source: We found that constitutive dbd silencing using TNT indeed resulted in longer, more branched lateral and medial A08a dendrites at 26±2 hr alh (Figure 4F–I).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite morphology shown in Figure 4F-I

claim: Silencing of dbd with Shibirets impaired larval crawling efficiency.
source: Silencing of dbd with Shibirets also impaired larval crawling efficiency (Figure 4C–E)
evidence: Behavioral analysis shown in Figure 4C-E

claim: Silencing of dbd with Shibirets resulted in longer, more branched A08a dendrites.
source: Silencing of dbd with Shibirets also impaired larval crawling efficiency (Figure 4C–E), and resulted in longer, more branched A08a dendrites (Figure 4J–M).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite morphology shown in Figure 4J-M

claim: Presynaptic activity from dbd is necessary to prevent excessive postsynaptic dendrite outgrowth in A08a.
source: Presynaptic activity from dbd is therefore necessary to prevent excessive postsynaptic dendrite outgrowth in A08a.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from TNT and Shibirets silencing experiments showing dendrite expansion

claim: CsChrimson-expressing larvae initiated fewer locomotor waves of activity.
source: We found that CsChrimson-expressing larvae initiated fewer locomotor waves of activity (Figure 5A–C)
evidence: Behavioral analysis shown in Figure 5A-C

claim: Activation of sensory neurons, including dbd, results in slowed larval locomotion.
source: We found that CsChrimson-expressing larvae initiated fewer locomotor waves of activity (Figure 5A–C), confirming a previous report that activation of sensory neurons, including dbd, results in slowed larval locomotion (Pulver et al., 2009).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Pulver et al., 2009

claim: dbd optogenetic activation led to a decrease in A08a dendrite length and branching.
source: After validating CsChrimson function, A08a dendrite length and complexity were assessed. Compared to negative controls expressing LacZ, dbd optogenetic activation led to a decrease in A08a dendrite length and branching.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite morphology shown in Figure 5D-G

claim: The effect of dbd optogenetic activation on dendrite reduction was most pronounced at the medial dendrite.
source: This effect was most pronounced at the medial dendrite; although some lateral arbors exhibited decreased length and branching, it did not reach statistical significance (Figure 5D–G).
evidence: Statistical analysis of dendrite measurements shown in Figure 5D-G

claim: Presynaptic activity is necessary and sufficient to restrict A08a dendrite outgrowth.
source: We conclude that presynaptic activity is necessary and sufficient to restrict A08a dendrite outgrowth.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from both silencing and activation experiments

claim: Neurons in many animals exhibit transient structural plasticity in early developmental windows that are termed 'critical periods' for plasticity.
source: Neurons in many animals exhibit transient structural plasticity in early developmental windows that are termed 'critical periods' for plasticity (Ackerman et al., 2021; Jarecki and Keshishian, 1995; LeVay et al., 1980; McLaughlin et al., 2003).
evidence: General statement supported by multiple citations

claim: In Drosophila larvae, motor neuron dendrites remain plastic until 8 hr alh.
source: In Drosophila larvae, motor neuron dendrites remain plastic until 8 hr alh, after which astrocytes prevent further dendritic remodeling, at least through 22 hr alh (Ackerman et al., 2021).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Ackerman et al., 2021

claim: After 8 hr alh, astrocytes prevent further dendritic remodeling in motor neurons, at least through 22 hr alh.
source: In Drosophila larvae, motor neuron dendrites remain plastic until 8 hr alh, after which astrocytes prevent further dendritic remodeling, at least through 22 hr alh (Ackerman et al., 2021).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Ackerman et al., 2021

claim: A08a was competent to expand its lateral dendrites only after dbd was ablated in newly hatched larvae at 0 hr alh.
source: In contrast, compared to negative controls (Figure 6D, F, H, J, L and M), we found that A08a was competent to expand its lateral dendrites only after dbd was ablated in newly hatched larvae at 0 hr alh (Figure 6F–G' and L–M)
evidence: Quantitative analysis of dendrite length after ablation at different timepoints shown in Figure 6L-M

claim: A08a lateral dendrites did not expand when dbd ablations occurred at 24 or 48 hr alh.
source: In contrast, compared to negative controls (Figure 6D, F, H, J, L and M), we found that A08a was competent to expand its lateral dendrites only after dbd was ablated in newly hatched larvae at 0 hr alh (Figure 6F–G' and L–M), but not when ablations occurred at 24 or 48 hr alh (Figure 6H–M).
evidence: Quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6H-M

claim: A08a dendrite structural plasticity is confined to an early critical period.
source: This result demonstrates that A08a dendrite structural plasticity is confined to an early critical period, perhaps the same critical period as used by the Drosophila larval motor system (Ackerman et al., 2021).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from temporal ablation experiments showing plasticity only at 0 hr alh

claim: Presynaptic contact is correlated with or promotes the local outgrowth of dendrites across a variety of model systems.
source: Across a variety of model systems, presynaptic contact is correlated with or promotes the local outgrowth of dendrites (Chen et al., 2010; Jacoby and Kimmel, 1982; Kamiyama et al., 2015; Niell et al., 2004; Vaughn, 1989).
evidence: General statement supported by multiple citations

claim: Ablation of sensory afferents resulted in failed M-cell dendrite formation in zebrafish and axolotl.
source: In classic studies performed on the giant Mauthner (M) cells in zebrafish and axolotl, ablation of sensory afferents resulted in failed M-cell dendrite formation, whereas suprainnervation by these afferents was sufficient to cause overelaboration of the M-cell dendrites (Goodman and Model, 1988; Kimmel et al., 1981; Kimmel et al., 1977).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from multiple studies on Mauthner cells

claim: Suprainnervation by sensory afferents was sufficient to cause overelaboration of the M-cell dendrites in zebrafish and axolotl.
source: In classic studies performed on the giant Mauthner (M) cells in zebrafish and axolotl, ablation of sensory afferents resulted in failed M-cell dendrite formation, whereas suprainnervation by these afferents was sufficient to cause overelaboration of the M-cell dendrites (Goodman and Model, 1988; Kimmel et al., 1981; Kimmel et al., 1977).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from multiple studies on Mauthner cells

claim: When paired with pharmacological silencing, suprainnervation of the M-cell still resulted in elongated dendrites, suggesting that contact-based cues are sufficient to drive local dendrite outgrowth.
source: Interestingly, when paired with a pharmacological silencing manipulation, suprainnervation of the M-cell still resulted in elongated dendrites, suggesting that contact-based cues are sufficient to drive local dendrite outgrowth (Goodman and Model, 1990)
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Goodman and Model, 1990

claim: The ability for an axon to promote local dendrite outgrowth offers a potential strategy for pre- and postsynaptic partner matching that is robust to variable axon positioning.
source: The ability for an axon to promote local dendrite outgrowth offers a potential strategy for pre- and postsynaptic partner matching that is robust to variable axon positioning.
evidence: Interpretation of the functional significance of contact-mediated dendrite outgrowth

claim: At the time of dbd CNS innervation at embryonic stage 14, the morphology of A08a dendrites is unknown.
source: At the time of dbd CNS innervation at embryonic stage 14, the morphology of A08a dendrites is unknown.
evidence: Statement acknowledging limitation of current tools for observing early A08a development

claim: It is unclear if dbd induces novel dendrite outgrowth from an otherwise bare neurite, or if it stabilizes and promotes continued dendrite elongation from an arbor already beginning to take form.
source: Therefore, it is unclear if dbd induces novel dendrite outgrowth from an otherwise bare neurite, or if it stabilizes and promotes continued dendrite elongation from an arbor already beginning to take form.
evidence: Statement acknowledging uncertainty about the mechanism of dendrite formation

claim: In wild-type animals, A08a dendrites are innervated by multiple neurons.
source: In wild-type animals, A08a dendrites are innervated by multiple neurons (Table 2; Sales et al., 2019).
evidence: Data from TEM connectome shown in Table 2 and previously published findings

claim: MP1 expresses the Dscam1 cell adhesion molecule.
source: MP1 expresses the Dscam1 cell adhesion molecule; presynaptic Dscam1 promotes the postsynaptic accumulation of Pak1 and Cdc42 in aCC, specifying the precise location of aCC dendrite elongation (Kamiyama et al., 2015; Wilhelm et al., 2022).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Kamiyama et al., 2015 and Wilhelm et al., 2022

claim: Presynaptic Dscam1 promotes the postsynaptic accumulation of Pak1 and Cdc42 in aCC, specifying the precise location of aCC dendrite elongation.
source: MP1 expresses the Dscam1 cell adhesion molecule; presynaptic Dscam1 promotes the postsynaptic accumulation of Pak1 and Cdc42 in aCC, specifying the precise location of aCC dendrite elongation (Kamiyama et al., 2015; Wilhelm et al., 2022).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Kamiyama et al., 2015 and Wilhelm et al., 2022

claim: Homeostatic structural plasticity is a phenomenon in which neurites adjust their length to counter the effect of too much or too little activity.
source: Homeostatic structural plasticity is a phenomenon in which neurites adjust their length to counter the effect of too much or too little activity; when activity is excessive, the dendrite shrinks, and when activity is diminished, the dendrite expands.
evidence: Definition of homeostatic structural plasticity based on established knowledge

claim: When activity is excessive, the dendrite shrinks, and when activity is diminished, the dendrite expands.
source: Homeostatic structural plasticity is a phenomenon in which neurites adjust their length to counter the effect of too much or too little activity; when activity is excessive, the dendrite shrinks, and when activity is diminished, the dendrite expands.
evidence: Definition of homeostatic structural plasticity based on established knowledge

claim: Homeostatic regulation of dendritic arbor size has been documented in insects and vertebrates.
source: Homeostatic regulation of dendritic arbor size has been documented in insects (Ackerman et al., 2021; Hoy et al., 1985; Tripodi et al., 2008; Yuan et al., 2011) and vertebrates (Shen et al., 2020; Takeo et al., 2021; Tanvir et al., 2021; Wu and Cline, 1998).
evidence: General statement supported by multiple citations from insect and vertebrate studies

claim: There is a homeostatic relationship between presynaptic activity levels and postsynaptic A08a dendrite length.
source: We observed a homeostatic relationship between presynaptic activity levels and postsynaptic A08a dendrite length.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments showing dendrite expansion with silencing and reduction with activation

claim: When synaptic input onto A08a was decreased by silencing evoked dbd activity, A08a dendrites were elongated.
source: When synaptic input onto A08a was decreased by silencing evoked dbd activity, A08a dendrites were elongated; when dbd was chronically activated, A08a dendrites were smaller.
evidence: Summary of experimental results from TNT and Shibirets experiments

claim: When dbd was chronically activated, A08a dendrites were smaller.
source: When synaptic input onto A08a was decreased by silencing evoked dbd activity, A08a dendrites were elongated; when dbd was chronically activated, A08a dendrites were smaller.
evidence: Summary of experimental results from CsChrimson experiments

claim: A08a dendrite length was modestly diminished in response to dbd stimulation.
source: In contrast to the robust effect of inhibiting dbd neurotransmission, A08a dendrite length was modestly diminished in response to dbd stimulation.
evidence: Observation from CsChrimson activation experiments

claim: The inhibitory A02d neuron is a top input to A08a.
source: One reason for this could be that the inhibitory A02d neuron, which is a top input to A08a (Table 2), also receives input from dbd (Table 1).
evidence: Data from TEM connectome shown in Tables 1 and 2

claim: A02d receives input from dbd.
source: One reason for this could be that the inhibitory A02d neuron, which is a top input to A08a (Table 2), also receives input from dbd (Table 1).
evidence: Data from TEM connectome shown in Table 1

claim: A02d could potentially cancel out some effects of dbd excitation in A08a.
source: A02d could therefore potentially cancel out some effects of dbd excitation in A08a.
evidence: Speculation about circuit interactions based on connectivity data

claim: Compensatory adjustments in dendrite length are likely a strategy to maintain a 'set-point' of synaptic input.
source: Compensatory adjustments in dendrite length are likely a strategy to maintain a 'set-point' of synaptic input.
evidence: Interpretation of the functional significance of homeostatic plasticity

claim: When dbd sensory innervation to the A08a medial dendrite was lost due to dbd ablation, A08a lateral dendrites were elongated whereas the medial arbor was maintained.
source: When dbd sensory innervation to the A08a medial dendrite was lost due to dbd ablation, A08a lateral dendrites were elongated whereas the medial arbor was maintained.
evidence: Summary of experimental results from dbd ablation experiments

claim: When dbd is ablated, A08a medial dendrites are unchanged due to the opposing roles of presynaptic activity and presynaptic contact.
source: We hypothesize that when dbd is ablated, A08a medial dendrites are unchanged due to the opposing roles of presynaptic activity and presynaptic contact.
evidence: Hypothesis proposed to explain the observation that medial dendrites don't change with ablation

claim: Lack of dbd contact restricts growth and lack of dbd activity promotes growth, working in direct opposition and resulting in no change in medial arbor size.
source: Lack of dbd contact (which restricts growth) and lack of dbd activity (which promotes growth) could be working in direct opposition and resulting in no change in medial arbor size.
evidence: Mechanistic explanation for why medial dendrites don't change with ablation

claim: The lateral arbor experiences only the loss of activity (which acts neuron-wide), leading to arbor growth.
source: In contrast, the lateral arbor experiences only the loss of activity (which acts neuron-wide), leading to arbor growth.
evidence: Mechanistic explanation for why lateral dendrites expand with ablation

claim: Presynaptic contact acts locally to promote dendrite outgrowth, whereas presynaptic activity acts globally across an entire neuron to downregulate dendrite elongation.
source: Taken together, our data support a model of dendrite development in which presynaptic contact acts locally to promote dendrite outgrowth, whereas presynaptic activity acts globally across an entire neuron to downregulate dendrite elongation (Figure 7).
evidence: Summary model based on all experimental results

claim: As synapses are added and become functional, activity could act as a negative-feedback mechanism to curb excessive dendrite elongation across the postsynaptic neuron.
source: We propose that as synapses are added and become functional, activity could act as a negative-feedback mechanism to curb excessive dendrite elongation across the postsynaptic neuron.
evidence: Proposed model for how activity regulates dendrite growth during development

claim: Sustained alterations to neurotransmission would likely impact postsynaptic calcium levels and therefore intracellular calcium signaling.
source: Sustained alterations to neurotransmission would likely impact postsynaptic calcium levels and therefore intracellular calcium signaling.
evidence: Speculation about molecular mechanisms based on established knowledge of neurotransmission

claim: Studies in Drosophila show PKA regulation of dendritic arbor size.
source: Indeed, studies in Drosophila show PKA regulation of dendritic arbor size (Baines, 2003; Tripodi et al., 2008).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Baines, 2003 and Tripodi et al., 2008

claim: Calcium can signal through regulators of transcription, allowing the effect of activity to potentially be exerted neuron-wide through changes in gene expression.
source: Calcium can also signal through regulators of transcription, allowing the effect of activity to potentially be exerted neuron-wide through changes in gene expression (Sun et al., 1994).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Sun et al., 1994

claim: Wnt signaling is recruited to inhibit dendrite elongation when activity levels are high.
source: For example, Wnt signaling is also recruited to inhibit dendrite elongation when activity levels are high (Singh et al., 2010).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Singh et al., 2010

claim: Critical periods are developmental windows of heightened neural plasticity that are present from vertebrates to insects.
source: Critical periods are developmental windows of heightened neural plasticity that are present from vertebrates (Kalb, 1994; Keck et al., 2017; Takesian and Hensch, 2013; Walton et al., 1992) to insects (Caglayan and Gilbert, 1987; Elekonich et al., 2003; Hartfelder et al., 1995; Levine et al., 1986; Morgan et al., 1998).
evidence: General statement supported by multiple citations from vertebrate and insect studies

claim: In Drosophila, critical periods have been identified in the late embryo/early larva and in the newly eclosed adult.
source: In Drosophila, critical periods have been identified in the late embryo/early larva (Ackerman et al., 2021; Crisp et al., 2011; Fushiki et al., 2013; Giachello et al., 2021; Giachello and Baines, 2015; Hartwig et al., 2008; Jarecki and Keshishian, 1995; Tripodi et al., 2008) and in the newly eclosed adult (Doll et al., 2017; Doll and Broadie, 2016; Doll and Broadie, 2015; Golovin et al., 2021; Golovin et al., 2019).
evidence: General statement supported by multiple citations

claim: Altered activity during the critical period can lead to long-lasting defects in neuronal morphology and behavior.
source: Altered activity during the critical period can lead to long-lasting defects in neuronal morphology and behavior (Ackerman et al., 2021; Crisp et al., 2011; Fushiki et al., 2013; Giachello et al., 2021; Giachello and Baines, 2015; Hartwig et al., 2008; Jarecki and Keshishian, 1995; Tripodi et al., 2008).
evidence: General statement supported by multiple citations

claim: In the Drosophila embryonic motor system, dendrite length can be homeostatically modified by levels of activity.
source: In the Drosophila embryonic motor system, dendrite length can be homeostatically modified by levels of activity (Tripodi et al., 2008).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Tripodi et al., 2008

claim: The motor dendrites lose the capacity to undergo activity-dependent remodeling at 8 hr alh, early in larval life.
source: The motor dendrites lose the capacity to undergo activity-dependent remodeling at 8 hr alh, early in larval life.
evidence: Previously published findings about motor neuron critical period

claim: The closure of the motor neuron critical period is governed by astrocytes.
source: The closure of this critical period is governed by astrocytes – their infiltration into the neuropil coincides with critical period closure and their contact with motor dendrites prevents precocious dendrite extension/retraction (Ackerman et al., 2021; Stork et al., 2014).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Ackerman et al., 2021 and Stork et al., 2014

claim: Astrocyte infiltration into the neuropil coincides with critical period closure.
source: The closure of this critical period is governed by astrocytes – their infiltration into the neuropil coincides with critical period closure and their contact with motor dendrites prevents precocious dendrite extension/retraction (Ackerman et al., 2021; Stork et al., 2014).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Ackerman et al., 2021 and Stork et al., 2014

claim: Astrocyte contact with motor dendrites prevents precocious dendrite extension/retraction.
source: The closure of this critical period is governed by astrocytes – their infiltration into the neuropil coincides with critical period closure and their contact with motor dendrites prevents precocious dendrite extension/retraction (Ackerman et al., 2021; Stork et al., 2014).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Ackerman et al., 2021 and Stork et al., 2014

claim: The larval nervous system continues to grow throughout its life, with individual neurons adding hundreds of microns of overall dendrite length.
source: The larval nervous system continues to grow throughout its life, with individual neurons adding hundreds of microns of overall dendrite length (Gerhard et al., 2017).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Gerhard et al., 2017

claim: Larval VNC neurons may generally be subject to the same early critical period regulated by astrocytes.
source: These results suggest that larval VNC neurons may generally be subject to the same early critical period regulated by astrocytes, and structural plasticity events may not be inducible in later stages of development.
evidence: Inference from the observation that A08a plasticity is limited to early larval life, similar to motor neurons

claim: Structural plasticity events may not be inducible in later stages of larval development.
source: These results suggest that larval VNC neurons may generally be subject to the same early critical period regulated by astrocytes, and structural plasticity events may not be inducible in later stages of development.
evidence: Inference from critical period experiments showing no plasticity after 24 hr alh

claim: A08a dendrite development is not hard-wired, but is modulated by the location of presynaptic partners and presynaptic activity levels.
source: Here and in previous work, we observed that A08a dendrite development is not hard-wired, but is modulated by the location of presynaptic partners and presynaptic activity levels (Sales et al., 2019; Valdes-Aleman et al., 2021).
evidence: Summary of findings from current and previous studies

claim: Natural variation in Drosophila melanogaster dorsal cluster neuron axonal projections directly impacts an animal's ability to orient toward a visual object.
source: For example, natural variation in Drosophila melanogaster dorsal cluster neuron axonal projections directly impacts an animal's ability to orient toward a visual object (Linneweber et al., 2020).
evidence: Previously published findings cited from Linneweber et al., 2020

claim: Imprecise but constrained morphological development could be a 'bet-hedging' strategy to promote the adaptability of an individual species to environmental changes.
source: Imprecise but constrained morphological development could be a 'bet-hedging' strategy to promote the adaptability of an individual species to environmental changes.
evidence: Speculation about the evolutionary significance of developmental variability

claim: For two highly divergent nematode species, Caenorhabditis elegans and Pristionchus pacificus, amphid sensilla neuron number and soma position are highly conserved whereas ciliated dendrite morphology is more diverse.
source: For two highly divergent nematode species, Caenorhabditis elegans and Pristionchus pacificus, amphid sensilla neuron number and soma position are highly conserved whereas ciliated dendrite morphology is more diverse.

claim: Neurons whose structure is more dissimilar between C. elegans and P. pacificus also have more divergent synaptic connections.
